title: Deterministic forced-offset reproduction of the early BIAS_OK assertion / POR_RAW release-then-reassert pulse (bias_core OK detector, real por_comparator + por_output_chain)
claim: Issue #495 -- NOT a spec claim (spec/target-spec.md has no ratified POR_RAW-glitch, ramp or reset row as of this record). Replaces the mismatch-seed reproduction of the ss/-40C mc14 pulse (PR #491 replay-474) with a deterministic forced offset: a DC source VOFF in series with the gate of ONE OK-detector device at a time -- XMOL2 (the output leg of the OK detector's XMOL1/XMOL2 mirror) or XMOKA (the OK-detector input device on NA, the XMOKA/XMOKB pair) -- in a DERIVED copy of design/netlist/bias_core.spice, swept over the per-grid offset_mv axes (pilot: XMOL2 -12..+12 mV and XMOKA -24..+24 mV; full: both devices -60..+36 mV; pilot-extended: XMOKA -120..+120 mV and XMOL2 -90..+90 mV), so the early-assertion / pulse behaviour has a repeatable testbench that does not depend on a mismatch seed. Every point is nominal-process (no _mm section): the offset is the only variation. Records, per point: the VDD at which BIAS_OK first asserts, every POR_RAW high interval on the UP segment other than the genuine release (pulse start/end VDD, width in volts and measured seconds), the genuine VPOR-up, and whether RESETn (real por_output_chain on the shared IBIAS) is released by a pulse. Each point is run under the default start, `uic`, and `gmin=1e-11` so solver-state dependence is stated, not assumed. Design and spec are unchanged.
provenance_source: sim/por-bias-ok-early-assert/testbench/tb_bias_ok_early_assert.sch (DUTs: design/netlist/por_comparator.spice, design/netlist/por_output_chain.spice, and design/netlist/bias_core.spice with the single-line VOFF/XMOL2- or VOFF/XMOKA-gate edit (the point's offset device) applied by run_early_assert.py)
statistical_convention: N/A (deterministic forced-offset sweep of the nominal drawn circuit, not a distribution claim). The offset axis is a sensitivity sweep; sigma_XMOL ~2.9 mV (issue #455) is used only to label +-3 sigma ~ +-9 mV input-referred.

devices.XMOL2: VOFF NOKLG NOKL DC {voff}; XMOL2 gate moved from NOKL to NOKLG (mirror output leg)
devices.XMOKA: VOFF NAG NA DC {voff}; XMOKA gate moved from NA to NAG (OK-detector input device; the XMOKA/XMOKB pair compares NA against NBTOP)

offset.sign: positive voff raises the named device's gate over its original node
offset.note: sigma_XMOL ~2.9 mV input-referred (issue #455); offsets beyond ~+-9 mV are >3 sigma and are swept only to bracket the onset, not as realistic draws

sweep.construction: V(VDD) = min(peak, rate*t, max(0, 2*peak - rate*t)); max time step = 2 mV of VDD (0.002/rate s) at every rate; total time 2*peak/rate

starts.default: tran with default initial condition (DC op first)
starts.uic: tran ... uic (the start the #474 MC campaign records use)

absent_coverage: Offsets are forced on ONE device at a time (XMOL2 or XMOKA, input-referred); joint/simultaneous multi-device offsets, direct offsets on the remaining OK-detector devices (XMOL1, XMOKB, XMOK2, XMOK2P, XMOKH), and global process Monte Carlo are NOT swept.
Mismatch Monte Carlo and post-layout parasitics are not run here (out of scope per #495).
The assembly is bias_core + por_comparator + por_output_chain on a shared IBIAS node, not temp_por_top: temp_core is not present, so its startup current draw is not on the supply.
Only the process/temperature pairs listed under grids.full.paired are run (the three binding-style corners), not the 15-point matrix; the subset reason is recorded in every record.
ngspice_note: Fleet ngspice may differ from the local one; the solver-state dependence this experiment probes means a local single-point cross-check is recorded beside the batch value.

classes.clean: one POR_RAW release on the UP ramp, no earlier pulse
classes.pulse_absorbed: one or more POR_RAW release-then-reassert pulses before the genuine release; RESETn is not released inside the pulse window (+2 ms settle)
classes.early_release: POR_RAW releases and STAYS high within 0.2 V of BIAS_OK's assertion (genuine release ~0.95 V higher in the controls), i.e. a premature release, not a pulse
classes.no_release: POR_RAW never releases on the UP ramp (BIAS_OK never asserts: the failed-release class of issue #455)
